key_insight: GLoC-EHR combines whole-record context and selected local EHR events to generate evidence-cited clinical answers that remain accurate while reducing unsupported reasoning.
clinical_relevance: For clinical NLP systems, this suggests that models can better answer record-based questions when they are trained to cite supporting EHR evidence rather than rely on direct generation alone.
method: Uses a fixed-size global memory to encode the full patient trajectory
Adds a local memory for selected events and masked concept descriptions
Trains with rationale fine-tuning and GRPO to reward correct, record-supported answers
evidence_signal: In three MIMIC-IV outcome tasks, GLoC-EHR achieved the highest macro AUROC among compared models in direct answering, and evidence-cited training kept performance close while reducing unsupported evidence; it also transferred to EHRSHOT on par with EHR-BERT.
watch_item: The evidence-citation gains depend on retraining and task-specific setup, so real-world deployment would need careful validation for reliability and strict evidence matching.
paper_title: GLoC-EHR: Evidence-Cited Clinical Reasoning over Global Context and Local EHR Events
